resources.string: Use this phone as a Bluetooth mouse for your computer. No software is needed on the computer.
Registering as a mouse and keyboard…
Simulated computer (debug build). Reports are recorded, not sent.
Boot mode (limited: no scrolling, media keys or buttons 4–5)

To act as a Bluetooth mouse, Mobile TrackPad needs the Nearby devices permission. It is used only to talk to computers you pair with and to make the phone visible during pairing. Notifications are optional: they show a Stop button while the trackpad is active.

1. Keep this screen open with the trackpad enabled.
2. Tap “Make phone visible for pairing”.
3. On the computer, open Bluetooth settings and add a new device. Choose this phone.
4. Confirm the pairing code on both devices if asked.

Pair only after enabling the trackpad. If this phone was paired with the computer before, remove the pairing on both the phone and the computer first, then pair again.
No paired devices. Pair the phone from the computer’s Bluetooth settings.
Grant the Nearby devices permission to see paired devices.
Paired while the trackpad was enabled.
Paired before the trackpad was enabled. If connecting fails, remove the pairing on both devices and pair again.
This computer removed the trackpad. Remove the pairing on both devices and pair again.
This phone does not report a Bluetooth adapter.
Turn on Bluetooth, then enable the trackpad again.

Bluetooth was turned off while the trackpad was enabled, so the session ended. On some phones this stops the trackpad from registering again until the phone restarts. If enabling fails after you turn Bluetooth back on, restart the phone. Next time, tap Stop before turning Bluetooth off.
The Nearby devices permission was not granted. Without it the app cannot act as a Bluetooth mouse.
Android did not allow the trackpad to start its background service. Open the app and tap Enable again.

Android did not provide its Bluetooth HID device service. Some phone manufacturers disable this feature. Try turning Bluetooth off and on, then try again. If it keeps failing, this phone may not support acting as a Bluetooth mouse.
Android refused to register the trackpad. Another app may currently be acting as a Bluetooth keyboard or mouse; close it and try again. Registration also fails if the app is not in the foreground.

Android accepted the request but never finished registering the trackpad. On some phones this happens after Bluetooth was turned off while the trackpad was enabled, and it lasts until the phone restarts. Restart the phone, then enable the trackpad again. While in this state the phone may also fail to connect to its own Bluetooth mice and keyboards.
Android ended the trackpad registration, for example because Bluetooth restarted or the app lost foreground priority. Enable it again.
The computer did not accept the connection. Check that its Bluetooth is on and it is in range. If it was paired before the trackpad was enabled, remove the pairing on both devices and pair again.
The computer did not respond in time. Check that it is awake, in range and has Bluetooth on, then try again.
The connection to the computer dropped. Held buttons were released on the phone. Connect again when ready.
The computer ended the virtual cable, which usually means it removed this device. Remove the pairing on the phone too, then pair again. The app will not reconnect automatically.
Each button sends standard mouse or media-key reports to the connected computer. Watch the computer and compare with what you expect.
Not connected. Connect to a computer first.
Holding is released automatically if you leave this screen, the phone screen turns off, or the connection drops.
Off by default. The log stays on this phone unless you copy or share it.
Shown while the phone is acting as a Bluetooth mouse.
